title: Skill procedures
description: Guides skill selection, invocation, specialist steps and handoffs while preserving project authority and recording boundaries.
responsibilities: Identify task fit, prepare applicable project context, and resolve resources needed by the selected invocation.
Guide the selected specialist activity and determine an applicable handoff using its governing inputs, limits, and assessments.
Prepare explicit recording operations and interpret actual command outcomes when governed recording is selected.

Consume IF-008 for the adopted-REM model-authoring branch of specialist guidance. Preserve governing source applicability and unresolved scope while retaining published invocation, specialist work, output presentation, and handoff responsibilities.

Compose requirement-first ownership and handoffs using separate Governance guidance, authority, evidence-support and work/adoption contracts. Keep actor-authored judgments distinct from the routing result.
owned_state: Published capability descriptions and procedural composition at the common invocation boundary; specialist methods, project state, authority, and evidence retain their own owners.

includes: Capability selection, portable invocation, conditional resource/evidence access, bounded specialist guidance, handoffs, and governed command use.
excludes: A hosted agent runtime, silently expanded invocation scope, package qualification from one successful invocation, mechanical record publication, or universal adoption of REM into installed skills.

design_limits: MOD-008 retains semantic authoring guidance behavior under MOD-017's IF-008 contract; MOD-006/007/009 retain shared authority, assurance, and learning meanings. Consuming guidance does not duplicate these responsibilities.

SCN-053 retains its guidance contract. SCN-075–082 now have selected guidance, authority, evidence-support and work/adoption cooperation and allocated workflow obligations; other specialist procedures and concrete implementation qualification remain outside this pass.
The current published capability output scope is not expanded by the new REM drafts. Actor-facing instruction packages remain distinct from agent execution and any public API.

The requirement-first workflow design supplies the selected SR-079–083 collaboration and AR allocation. Earlier broader deferrals remain only outside that bounded extension; existing runtime observations and installed contracts do not implement the target design.

sources.basis: Proposed responsibility derived from the published-product source inventory. Existing Designs retain their detailed contracts; this allocation is not a runtime migration or approval.

sources.locator: MOD-012; SCN-019, SCN-053, SCN-066 selected collaboration analysis
sources.basis: Derive consumer-focused parent contracts for selected-state inspection, adopted-REM authoring guidance, applicable action authority, and evidence applicability. Preserve child behavior/state authority, existing Function/AR allocations, and earlier contract guarantees. The selected contracts refine prior blanket deferrals; remaining retention, wider collaboration, AR, and realization gaps stay explicit. This is draft design analysis, not implemented or satisfied behavior.

sources.locator: MOD-012 realization/software.json public entries and proposed Function correspondence
sources.basis: The catalog records public skill names and partial proposed contributions without changing Function allocation, specialist contract ownership, published output support, or runtime qualification. Complete specialist realization remains deferred.
Draft integrated design from the accepted requirement-first basis. This defines target responsibility and cooperation, not installed capability, design approval, runtime evidence or SQLite adoption.
